thread:
oncall-bot: Paging oncall — high error rate (500s) from serving runtime in us-west-2. Autoscaler event storm detected. Impact: API latency spikes, some customer requests failing. Please ACK and start triage.

matt: ACKing. joining. seeing lots of cuda out-of-memory in logs.

matt: quick paste of error from one pod:
```
E tensorflow: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: out of memory
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z handler: runtime: failed to allocate KV cache
container restart backoff
```

nora: also seeing rapid pod churn — HPA scaled replicas from 8 -> 42 in ~3m then back down. node additions flapping. suspect autoscaler cooldown too low.

ryan: my view: node provisioning latency + immediate eviction causes pods to rebind to new nodes then crash on first GPU allocation. Crashloop increases observed GPU pressure. Autoscaler treats crashloops as demand and keeps scaling up -> yo-yo.

infra-sre: on it. temporarily pausing cluster-autoscaler for the affected ASG, setting max nodes to current to stop further scale-up. Recommend setting scaleDownDelay and cooldown to avoid immediate tear-down.

matt: applying taint to new nodes to prevent scheduling of heavy infer pods while we stabilize: `kubectl taint nodes <node> infer-stabilize=true:NoSchedule` — patching daemon to avoid eviction.

ryan: also rolling back the recent GPU driver update in the staging pool? Any change sets that could change memory allocator behaviour?

matt: noted. no driver roll in prod this morning. but one model rollout yesterday increased token length default which moves memory profile up. pushing patch to limit max_input_len for that model as emergency.

elaine: CS here. we have two customers on Dedicated experiencing errors. drafting a terse comms item: "We're investigating increased 500s; temporary mitigation in progress; no data loss expected. ETA next update 30m." Want me to send now?

customer-success-bot: Template ready: `Impact, Mitigation, ETA`. Queueing send on approval.

qa-jen: running quick smoke across canary endpoints to check degraded models and confirm fallback behavior.

matt: update: found repeated `cudaMalloc` failures with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` followed by OOM. Stack traces vary by model. Example block:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.0 GiB (GPU 0; 14.73 GiB total capacity; 12.2 GiB already allocated)
  File "/srv/runtime/engine/alloc.cpp", line 312, in allocate
```

nora: metrics: GPU utilization spikes to 96% during the flapping, with GPU memory fragmentation growing across older pods. Autoscaler decisions are based on CPU+mem at node level — it doesn't see per-GPU fragmentation.

infra-sre: tactical plan proposal:
1) pause autoscaler (done)
2) cordon and drain a few suspect nodes and restart kubelet/driver
3) limit new deployments of large-context models via a routing rule to dedicated pool
4) lower HPA max replicas for the next 30m
5) monitor p99 latency and 500-rate

ryan: executing step 2 now — `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` - doing one at a time.

matt: applying a temporary scaling-profile on serving runtime to reduce batch size: `BATCH_MAX=8` to lower transient memory usage.

elaine: sending customer ping now. keeping it conservative.

oncall-bot: Incident update — autoscaler paused at 09:20 UTC. Manual node operations in flight. Next update in 10m or on milestone.

qa-jen: smoke results: fallbacks triggered correctly for 3/4 flows; one route still failing at high token lengths. isolating which model config overrides are missing.

matt: found one expired quantization cache that causes increased allocation peaks when loaded. clearing caches on nodes as part of restart.

ryan: node restart sequence done for 4 nodes. observed lower fragmentation after warmup. memory avail on GPU increased ~1.5 GiB on average.

infra-sre: after restarting and tainting, we see stability. p95 latency trending down from 1.8s -> 480ms. 500-rate reduced to baseline.

matt: re-enabled autoscaler with conservative limits: min 8 max 18, scale-up cooldown 240s, scale-down-delay 600s. HPA max replicas lowered to 20. removing taints gradually.

nora: monitoring will show if crashloops reappear. setting alert for consecutive OOM errors > 3 within 2m.

elaine: update to impacted customers sent: "Mitigation applied; reduced impact; continuing to monitor; support on standby." Customers acknowledged, one asked for postmortem.

customer-success-bot: Logged customer contacts and ticked support follow-up.

matt: postmortem checklist: collect driver and container logs, autoscaler events, HPA events, node provisioning timeline, rollout metadata for models served 09:00-09:30. Assigning to @matt for write-up and @nora for autoscaler config review.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved? Current status: stable. Will keep on watch for 1h. If no regressions, we close and start postmortem.

ryan: confirmed 1h watch agreed. congratulations team. :tada:

elaine: I'll coordinate postmortem comms and schedule a customer follow-up call if needed.

matt: final note — root cause likely combination: model change increasing peak memory + cache fragmentation + autoscaler reacting to transient pod crashes -> scale yo-yo. remediation: autoscaler tuning, model max_length guardrails, improved GPU mem fragmentation metrics, and a preflight for driver/cache lifecycle on node add.

nora: adding action item: add per-GPU memory fragmentation metric to alerting and evaluate using specialized bin-packing for GPUs.

oncall-bot: Closing incident channel for active mitigation. Thread will be used for postmortem drafts and action items. Timestamp end 3467103000.
